prev_card.title: You found the painting
prev_card.html:
The photo was taken at the port of Le Havre. The police stopped crate CR-017 there at 00:35. The Mona Lisa is safe.

The data term: Metadata

Metadata is data about data. The phone wrote its model, the time and the position into the photo file. The sender never typed them, and probably never knew they were there.

What you did with data

Data is a badge number and a time. Information is that badge belonging to Julien Moreau, at the corridor door, during the speeches. Knowledge is understanding what happened, well enough to send police to a port.

  • Collect: files you were given, an API you asked, metadata you found inside a photo.
  • Process: filter, join on an ID, and correct a clock.
  • Publish: the timeline above, which anyone can check against the records.

Three wrong assumptions

  • "Logistics moves crates, so it was the logistics coordinator." A role is not evidence.
  • "The time on the picture is the time." Every clock belongs to a device, and a device can run fast or slow.
  • "His workstation, so him." True this time, but only the door log made it so.

Nothing in this case was hacked. One person used the rights that came with his job. More about that in the week on security and privacy.
